title: Recipes home — choose the composition
question: The visual world is fixed (lime/navy/cream, Plus Jakarta Sans, illustration-forward). This choice is structure only, for the style-setting Recipes tab. The roll leads with the Cookbook index.

options.label: Cookbook Index
options.lineage: the index pages of a working cookbook
options.thesis: The recipe shelf as a dense, scannable index — every row a complete fact: illustration, title, time, allergens, provenance.
options.viewport: Masthead 'Rezepte', a restrained September-drop banner with Plus chip, category chip row, then editorial list rows: 4:3 illustration left, title/meta/allergen glyphs/provenance badge right. Tab bar with visible labels.
options.risk: The monthly drop reads quieter than 'featured on top' ambition — the banner must earn attention through illustration, not size.

raised.raise: Sections hold as strict horizontal bands; every state named in text, never color alone.

regions.label: tab bar · Recipes Builder Shopping Pantry More

options.label: Utility First
options.lineage: the tool wall of a well-run kitchen
options.thesis: Search and categories lead; the drop and the grid follow — the tab opens as a tool, not a magazine.
options.viewport: Search field on top, a 3×2 illustrated category tile grid, the September-drop card mid-screen with Plus chip, then a 2-column recipe grid. Tab bar with visible labels.
options.risk: A tool-first opening cools the warm domestic temperament — reads instrument-panel unless the tiles carry real illustration warmth.

options.label: Monthly Cover
options.lineage: a baking periodical's monthly cover on the kitchen shelf
options.thesis: The September drop is the cover of the month — one tall illustrated card owns the opening viewport; the cadence is the brand.
options.viewport: Masthead 'September-Drop', a tall cover card (~40% of viewport) with the drop's illustration, Plus chip and provenance badge, caption anchored low; category chips; 2-column illustrated grid below. Tab bar with visible labels.
options.risk: The cover pushes the browsing grid below the fold — regular users pay one extra scroll every visit.

raised.raise: The cover card commits fully — illustration owns the card edge to edge, caption and badges anchored low, nothing floating mid-card.
